checks.title: Alert identity
checks.detail: Opened the alert and checked it was still active.

checks.title: Rule reason
checks.detail: Read the alert's reason to see what fired it.

checks.title: Source evidence
checks.detail: Followed the alert to its source evidence to confirm ${truth.finding}.

answer.evidence: The alert and the matching source event show that it is ${truth.finding}, with ${truth.scope}.

goals.title: Open this run's alert
goals.concept: An alert's status only means something together with its rule's reason and the time it ran.
goals.narration: Find and open the alert created for this exercise.
goals.reasoning: This run's own rule keeps other, older alerts out of the picture.
goals.evidence: The alert detail belongs to this run.

demonstration.narration: I'll open this run's alert so we can check the rule that actually fired before judging its impact.
demonstration.reasoning: The Alerts table can hold alerts from other rules and times. Opening this run’s row keeps that history out of the decision.
demonstration.evidence: The highlighted title and status show this is ${var.alert} and that it is still active. The Reason says what crossed the threshold, but status alone doesn't yet prove customer impact.

hints: Start with the alert created for this exercise.
Use the Alerts table and its rule names.
Open ${var.alert}; Show me can do it for you.

drifts.note: You opened ${action.value}; that alert belongs to a different rule.

goals.title: Read the status and reason
goals.concept: Status says whether the condition still holds; reason explains what crossed the threshold.
goals.narration: Read the alert's reason and its recent history.
goals.reasoning: A fired rule is not automatically a current customer incident.
goals.evidence: The reason and timing show the alert's condition.

demonstration.narration: I'll open Alert details to read its status and Reason. They show whether the condition still holds, and what crossed the threshold.
demonstration.reasoning: A rule may have fired earlier, recovered, or matched harmless data. Read its current status and reason before deciding what the alert means.
demonstration.evidence: The status is still Active, and the highlighted Reason gives the count that crossed the threshold. A source event still has to confirm the impact.

hints: Separate the rule state from its interpretation.
Open the alert's details page to read its Reason, status and recent history.
Open the alert reason; Show me can point it out.

goals.title: Pivot to the source evidence
goals.concept: Triage requires a source event, trace, or metric beyond the alert itself.
goals.narration: Follow the alert to matching source evidence.
goals.reasoning: The pivot shows whether the condition really means customers are affected.
goals.evidence: The source result backs up the triage decision.

demonstration.narration: I'll use View in Discover to open the documents the rule matched. Real events should back up the alert's claim of customer impact.
demonstration.reasoning: An alert is built from other data. Pivoting means following it to that data, so the condition is tested against real events, not just the alert's title.
demonstration.evidence: This is one of the documents the rule matched, and its highlighted fields show a real failure behind the alert. ${truth.conclusion}

hints: Don't judge the alert from its title alone.
On the alert's details page, View in Discover opens the documents its rule matched.
Pivot to the source evidence; Show me can do it for you.

goals.title: Submit the triage decision
goals.concept: Decide the state and priority, then point to the evidence for your choice.
goals.reasoning: A priority you can defend links the alert to its effect on customers.
goals.evidence: The answer points to the alert and the source evidence.
hints: Decide whether the alert still describes customer impact, has recovered, or is noise, and set a priority.
Use the coach's triage form: your decision, its priority and scope, and why.
Submit your decision, the priority and your reasons; Show me shows the reference summary.
